templates.text: A sudden, sharp clap → a full-body startle, followed by a brief, high-pitched cry.
A sustained, moderate-volume hum → head turns slowly toward the source, limbs become still.
A rhythmic tapping sound → eyes blink in synchrony, hands make small grasping motions.
A nearby, abrupt cough → arms fling outward in the Moro reflex, then slowly retract.
A low-frequency rumble → the baby's breathing pattern briefly hitches, brows furrow.
A repetitive, mid-pitch beep → quiet vocal cooing begins, matching the beep's tempo.
A sudden hiss of air → the infant startles, then orients mouth toward the sound source.
A gentle, shushing sound → crying ceases, the baby's eyes open wide and search.
A crisp paper crinkle → legs draw up in a brief fencing posture, then relax.
A distant, moderate siren → the newborn becomes alert and still, with increased heart rate.
A metallic clang → a sharp inhalation, followed by a delayed, short cry after {seconds} seconds.
A steady dripping noise → sucking motions begin without an object, hands move to mouth.
An unexpected door click → the rooting reflex is triggered, head turns side to side.
A human voice speaking softly → the baby's gaze fixes, and minor limb jerks subside.
A moderate-volume bell ring → eyes widen, then squint, arms exhibit a brief tremor.
A burst of white noise → the infant arches its back slightly, then settles into stillness.
A sequence of three soft knocks → breathing pauses, then resumes at a faster rate.
A mid-range musical note → facial muscles relax, a subtle smile reflex appears briefly.
A plastic bottle being squeezed → the head turns away, and one arm extends in a protective gesture.
A steady, moderate fan motor → the baby's eyes close, but limbs remain toned and ready.
A quick, sharp whistle → the Moro reflex initiates partially, followed by a sigh.
A recording of a heartbeat → fussing movements cease, the infant's posture becomes more flexed.
A sudden book page turn → a blink, followed by a slow, searching head rotation.
A moderate dog bark → a full startle, then crying builds over {seconds} seconds.
A consistent metronome tick → foot and hand movements become rhythmically aligned.
A vacuum cleaner starts → the baby gasps, limbs stiffen, and the cry is momentarily suppressed.
A light switch flicking on → the infant blinks rapidly, then stares toward the ceiling.
A moderate rain patter → sucking intensity on a pacifier increases, eyes remain closed.
A chair scraping the floor → a brief, whole-body jerk, followed by a quiet whimper.
A human sneeze → the startle reflex is elicited, followed by a brief period of wide-eyed alertness.
